_meta.purpose: CULINARY_PREFERENCE records. How a cook likes a steak, chop or fillet. These are not safety statements. Any tier that sits below the matching SAFETY_MINIMUM carries below_safety_minimum: true and the renderer must print the disclosure sentence next to it.
_meta.two_layers: Industry bodies (Beef Board, American Lamb Board) publish doneness scales that START at the USDA minimum: medium-rare is a 145 F final. Steakhouse and pitmaster convention runs lower (rare 120-125 F). Both are recorded. The industry layer is SOURCED; the convention layer is NEEDS_SOURCE and flagged below the minimum. Neither is a safety claim.
_meta.disclosure_default: Rare, medium-rare and medium figures are culinary preference ranges that fall below the USDA FSIS safe minimum of 145 F with a 3 minute rest. USDA does not consider them safe. Where the two differ, the USDA minimum governs.

records.scope: steaks and roasts, final temperature after rest
records.carryover: Roasts rise 5 to 15 F after leaving the heat; allow 15 to 20 minutes standing time.
notes: This is the Beef Checkoff's published scale. It aligns with USDA and is the scale Pit Log prints by default on beef pages.

records.scope: steaks, steakhouse and pitmaster convention, pull temperatures
records.carryover: Craft convention: 5 to 10 F rise on a steak during a 5 to 10 minute rest.
records.disclosure: Rare, medium-rare and medium figures are culinary preference ranges that fall below the USDA FSIS safe minimum of 145 F with a 3 minute rest. USDA does not consider them safe. Where the two differ, the USDA minimum governs.
notes: These are the figures the beef master prints. No federal or industry body publishes them; they are convention. They may render only with the disclosure and only alongside doneness-beef-industry.
A tier-2 or tier-3 source for the convention scale has not been located. Until one is, review_status stays NEEDS_SOURCE and the beef page leads with the industry scale.

records.scope: chops, rack, leg and roasts. Pull temperature and final temperature after rest
records.carryover: American Lamb Board: pull 10 F below the target because the internal temperature keeps rising.
notes: Applied to goat on the FSIS statement that goat cuts are similar to lamb; no goat industry scale exists.
The pull figure of 135 F is a pull, not a final. A surface may print it only as 'pull at 135, final 145 after rest'.

records.scope: chops and rack, restaurant convention, pull temperatures
records.carryover: 5 to 10 F on a rack or chop.
records.disclosure: Rare, medium-rare and medium figures are culinary preference ranges that fall below the USDA FSIS safe minimum of 145 F with a 3 minute rest. USDA does not consider them safe. Where the two differ, the USDA minimum governs.
notes: These are the figures on the lamb and goat masters. The masters do not flag them as below the minimum; that is a graphics defect logged in graphics/masters.json.
The lamb master's 'magic range 130-145 F for most lamb cuts' is a convention claim that contradicts the American Lamb Board's own scale. Do not reproduce it.

records.scope: chops, loin, tenderloin and whole-muscle roasts
records.carryover: National Pork Board: pull a smoked loin at 140 F and rest 10 minutes in a warm place until it reaches 145 F. Chops: 145 F then a 3 minute rest.
notes: Pork at 145 F is often still pink. That is safe and normal (FSIS).

The Pork Board's 'pull at 140, rest to 145' is a carryover technique whose FINAL reading is the USDA minimum. A surface may only print it with the final figure. Never print 140 F as a pork target on its own.

records.carryover: Salmon carries over 5 to 10 F after a short rest; a fillet pulled at 140 F commonly reads 145 F at the table, but only the reading counts.
records.disclosure: Every salmon figure below 145 F is a culinary preference that falls below the USDA FSIS and FDA safe minimum of 145 F. Where the two differ, the federal minimum governs.
notes: The salmon master's 'Pull at 135-140 F for juicy, flaky results' describes a preference below the minimum and must not render as advice without the disclosure.
FDA visual cue at the minimum: flesh opaque and separates easily with a fork.

records.carryover: A whole bird rises several degrees during a 10 minute rest; the rest is for juiciness, USDA requires none.
notes: Cooking dark meat past 165 F is a texture preference: connective tissue renders and the meat firms. It is above the minimum, so it needs no disclosure, but it is still convention and not USDA guidance.
Breast meat: 165 F is both the minimum and the practical ceiling for juiciness. The chicken-A master's 'pull at 160-165 F' is BELOW the minimum at its low end and is logged as a safety defect.
